What is the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis code for this patient?

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Age: 69
Sex: Male
Date of Admission: [REDACTED]
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient was admitted with severely symptomatic atrial fibrillation (AF) requiring multiple cardioversions. He had a history of an implantable cardiac monitor, left bundle branch block with an ejection fraction of 25%, and a cardiac resynchronization therapy device (CRT-D). The patient underwent uncomplicated pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) using radiofrequency (RF) via the SANS FLUORO technique. There were no complications during or after the procedure. The patient was discharged the following day and remained free of AF at his three- and six-month follow-up visits.

HISTORY AND FINDINGS:
The patient had previously undergone successful implantation of the Optimizer™ III device as part of a clinical trial. The preprocedure chest radiograph showed increased scar burden in the left atrium (LA) based on voltage mapping, with ablation lesions showing the left atrial roof and posterior line. Post-PVI, entrance and exit blocks were demonstrated. The postprocedure CRT-D check revealed no change in lead sensing, threshold, or impedance values.
DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
PROCEDURE/TREATMENT:
Uncomplicated pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) using radiofrequency (RF) via the SANS FLUORO technique.

FOLLOW-UP:
The patient remained free of AF at his three- and six-month follow-up visits.

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
The patient is instructed to follow up with their healthcare provider as recommended.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
N/A

DISCHARGE CONDITION:
The patient was discharged in stable condition.

text:
# Principal Diagnosis: **I48.9 – Atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter, unspecified**

## Why atrial fibrillation is the principal diagnosis
- The patient was admitted for severely symptomatic atrial fibrillation.
- The procedure performed (radiofrequency pulmonary vein isolation) was done specifically to treat the AF.
- Under ACS 0001 (Principal Diagnosis), this is the condition chiefly responsible for the admission.

## Why the unspecified code
- ICD-10-AM divides AF into paroxysmal (I48.0), persistent (I48.1) and permanent (I48.2).
- The record does not state which type this is.
- "Requiring multiple cardioversions" suggests persistent AF, since AF that needs cardioversion is not self-terminating. However, coders should not assign a type the clinician has not documented.
- A clinician query is recommended. If the AF is confirmed as **persistent**, assign **I48.1** instead.

## Likely additional diagnosis codes
| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| I44.7 | Left bundle-branch block, unspecified |
| I50.9 / I50.1 | Heart failure / left ventricular failure (EF 25%), if clinically documented as heart failure |
| Z95.0 | Presence of cardiac pacemaker (covers the CRT-D) |
| Z95.8 | Presence of other cardiac and vascular implants and grafts (implantable cardiac monitor, Optimizer device) |

## Procedure
Code the radiofrequency pulmonary vein isolation with the ACHI code for percutaneous ablation of the atrium/pulmonary vein. This falls within block 601, for example **38287-02**, depending on the ACHI edition in use.
